reviews.comment: Do not worry if you get stuck with professor Olga. I had no high school AP physics experience and I did ok. Lectures are not helpful so I learned most of the material through the homework. The recitation is quite useful. However, she encourages students to ask any questions through email or office hours as she is very willing to help.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Excellent lecturer when I had her. She spoiled me by helping me all the time whenever I had physics problems or questions. Olga is a very knowledgeable and correcting yet caring lecturer who encourages you to keep learning!

She does her best, but she is a super genius who does not speak english well. Take Michael Youngs or another prof please it doesnt matter how bad your schedule is. The class is just hard in general, but with her it is likely you will not get an A. Very difficult, I do not recommend her

She is a pretty bad lecturer, even past the accent which I don't think is that bad, but she faces the board when she talks and doesn't turn around until switching slides. Speaking of the slides, they break almost every rule of making a good slideshow, and could only be worse if her slides were in a different language.

She is a very caring lady, but it is extremely difficult to understand her and her handwriting during lecture. Her slides are absolutely horrendous and cluttered. Most of your learning will probably be done through the homework and past exam repository. I do not recommend taking her unless you already have a good grasp on mechanics.

While she is a nice professor, she is impossible to understand during her lectures. Time in class is better spent doing homework than listening to the lecture material. Everything I learned in this class was from the textbook and in my own time. Take her if you can learn on your own.

Olga is a very nice lady but I had to stop trying to pay attention in her lectures a few weeks in. She tends to overcomplicate things. University Physics is kind of self explanatory since you just use the equations so I never really bothered to learn outside of class. I just attended for the iClicker than did other homework.

She's a nice enough person and kinda funny but her lectures are a bit of a mess, she goes through material very quickly but with an accent you can hardly understand. Take literally anyone else or attend other professors lectures, that's what I ended up doing and it saved my grade
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Practically incomprehensible accent, slides are a cluttered mess, and her handwriting is garbage. Take any other professor for University Phys if you can manage, and use your mandatory lecture time to work on homework.

Dr Kocharovskaya was horrendous at teaching the material IMO. She convolutes the lecture material, has terrible organized slides, and has a hard time communicating through her thick accent. I ended up using Organic Chemistry Tutor and other online resources instead of going to class. Terrible professor for such a difficult course.

Its all basically using formulas without the intuition behind them but being tested on the understanding of them. She sometimes lectures well on the examples but its 50/50 for that.  All of that could be forgiven if there wasn't just so much work. I'm in 2 Math 4xx's right now and have less work in both of those courses combined than this course.

I really have no idea how some professors get jobs. I understand that this material is tough on its own, and it doesn't help that this professor can barely speak English. You can barely hear her and she just scribbles on the white board the whole class. And of course, attendance is graded so you're forced to come in and waste your time not learning

Physics 207 is a difficult class but Professor Kocharovskaya makes it even worse. Her lectures are impossible to follow. She just work out difficult physics problems and assumes the students understand. 
Attendance is mandatory since every lecture includes iClicker assignments. Do yourself a favor and take any other professor for physics.

Rarely there comes a prof of this low caliber. Her idea of class participation involves clicker questions where you have to use formulas and concepts you just learned in under a minute. If you can't pick up a new concept explained with an incomprehensible Russian accent and immediately apply it to problems in under a minute, then dodge this prof

PHYS 207 is just a difficult class there is a lot of content that has to be shoved into the semester, but she tries to explain it and actually seems to care that you understand the concepts. The test review powerpoints are usually very similar to the test themselves and are a good resource. The in class polls go by quickly so pay attention.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: STAY AWAY FROM THIS PROFESSOR! Her slides are confusing/packed with non-important info and her accent makes much of what she's saying hard to decipher. HW will take up all your time. Clicker quizzes are too hard to finish in one minute. I've had to self-teach my way through this class because of how bad the slides are and how rushed lecture feels.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Isn't a terrible professor, but she has a very thick accent and often rambles when solving examples during lectures. I learned most of the material from the prelectures and recitation. iClicker questions every class, she gives a minute for every question then doesn't explain the problem even when <50% get it right. The course is curved though.

This course is not the easiest. But she does her best to explain the concepts really well. Her lecture slides are also really helpful. Do not go by the low rating, according to me it is just because the course is a bit rigorous. I would say she does an excellent job and it shows that she genuinely cares about her students.

Hardest class I've ever taken so far as a sophomore in engineering. The curriculum is super hard and it's not Olga's fault, but her accent is very thick. The curve for Fall 2020 was 55 overall for a C, 74 for a B, and 87 for A. Take Don't Panic and don't think twice.

I took physics 207 with her online. She isnt the best at giving lectures especially over zoom, but her slides were good for reviewing for the exams. Make sure to attend class for clicker questions. She does a really good job of putting whats gonna be on the test on review slides, memorize clicker answers. She is nice about pushing hw back. Hard.

Hard class, but Olga made it better. I relied primarily on tutoring because the teaching style fits me better, not because she was a bad professor. Always available outside of class and really tries to get students to understand. However, she does have Clicker questions in class where 30 seconds feel like 8 seconds.

The class is hard, but she clearly cares about her students and wants them to pass. I took Vitaly the semester before, and her accent is nothing compared to his. Would definitely recommend going to SI sessions. Half the questions on the final are identical to the previous finals before, so study those. Clicker questions make attendance mandatory.

She is very kind. However, the course is extremely difficult so it won't be easy to pass. The only thing that I had a hard time with her was her accent. Very thick and hard to understand. Although I went to her lectures for clickers, I didn't really pay attention to what I was learning before the homework.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She learned physics in high school, so she does not understand what the students no understand. The course is designed weirdly, like requiring 2nd and 3rd integral which you will learn in later coursework. Naturally, a badly designed course with the too smart professor doesn't work well. However, she is really nice and smart, and accessible.

This course is one of the toughest at A&M and there really isn't much you can do about it. From my understanding none of the other professors (except for ones who teach Don't Panic) were that great either. The general structure of this course makes it hard for anyone to pass.
A sweet lady that knows her stuff, but her accent is thick and she assumes concepts are simple even when they're first introduced. Super helpful in office hours.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: 208 IS Not as bad as the rumors they make out of it .Cant say olga is a horrible proffesor because i barely come to class lol but i either made an A/B for this course. gO TO A+ tutoring. if you dont want a B then take it at blinn

Since 208 is a common course, Olga doesn't get a ton of control over the exams or the assigned homework. However, she is fully in charge of her own lectures, and she does a pretty good job of lecturing on the chapters. She's a sweetie, not difficult to understand. Read the chapter before class, pay attention during class, and you'll survive 208.

Prof. Olga (I called her my "Babushka" throughout the semester) is insanely knowledgeable & distinguished. She's coauthored papers with Nobel Prize winners & has globally-respected laser research. The class is hard, but the course if very logically organized. Do the work, go to lecture, ask her for help if you need it, and you'll be fine.

If you thought 218 was bad, get ready for 208. In general, all the profs are bad. Olga is really nice and cares about what she teaches, but she can't dumb it down enough for non-physics people to understand. The tests are rough and the grading system for this course is a nightmare. Just don't take this course at A&M, but if you have to, avoid Olga.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: In general, 208 is a class you want to avoid taking at A&M at all costs. Olga doesn't make it any better. She can't teach down to the level of students. She is not helpful during office hours and often makes you feel dumb. She also does very complicated examples that are hard to follow. Just don't take this class here
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not a good teacher. She is nice and helpful and a very well respected researcher but not cut out for teaching. I learned everything in recitation or on youtube because the lectures were not helpful whatsoever. Very difficult class conceptually, do yourself a favor and don't take her.

Olga is sweet and a genius in her field, but she is not cut out for teaching. She lacks the ability to meet her students' needs as an instructor. Unless you want to spend your weekends reading the textbook to get a 50 or below on a test (where 50 is the average), DO NOT take her. Take this class with a different professor or outside of A&M.

Hard class and the mandatory lectures, I did not find her office hours, lab, or lecture help much so I recommend reading the book and attending tutoring. The class is based off learning objectives and concepts. The average grade in my class is a 58 so she had to change the grade distribution. 100-85 A 84-60 b 60-40 c

Dr. Kocharovskaya wants everyone to understand the material of the course. She is always willing to answer questions and help if you struggle. Her lectures are informative and she posts lectures slides. A lot of online homework but it helps to prepare for exams.  She has an accent but its pretty understandable.

She is very knowledgeable in her field and her experience shows. She might take a couple of weeks to get used to but a combination of just going to her lectures and her office hours (which is astoundingly useful) should makes things a lot easier.

Great person, really cares that students learn and try their best, willing to help in office hours. Course content is difficult and there is a lot of extra homework that doesn't seem to help understanding. Olga is really smart and sometimes goes too fast in lecture. Studying previous exams will help the most in the class.

208 is hard no matter the professor, however she is very hard to understand at times. Lecture didn't do much for me, nor did recitation. I learned a lot through the book before tests. The HW was insane (mastering, flip-it, prelectures, pre-ICE) because there was so much EACH week. That is not her fault though. She isn't the best but does care alot.

PHYS 208 at at Texas A&M is difficult no matter which professor you have. Don't change your schedule around to avoid Dr. Kocharovskaya. She is a very nice professor,  never annoyed by questions, and is often very generous in giving points back on exams . Unfortunately she is hard to follow in lecture, definitely buy the book and read it thoroughly.
Hardest class you will ever take.  The drop rate is extremely high and this class makes you rethink your life's choices.

Olga is a physics genius, and a really nice lady. But she's not a good teacher. A lot of students have a hard time understanding what she's saying and writing, and you're not going to learn anything from lectures. Exams are hard, but fair. She's not a bad professor to have for 208, but you should go to A+  if you want to pass the course.

She does clicker questions at beginning of very lecture. Also her lectures will lose you in all the math. Very hard to understand. Usually does give points back on test if you go to her office hours. She does try to help you learn what you've done wrong on the test in office hours but she is just very hard to understand. Overall just a hard class.
I recommend an A+ tutoring pass. You won't regret it. She is a nice, sweet lady. I never failed a test but most people do. 208 will be hard no matter what, READ THE BOOK. REALLY UNDERSTAND IT.
Her lectures do not flow well, at times very confusing.  Most of the time not understandable. Better to just read the book and not waste time with her yawn-inducing lectures.
